whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the AFC-1006 CI push-trigger one-liner. The CTO is the author of both paths listed below. This claim asserts authorship and paths; it asserts nothing about whether the change is correct. R2 is pending: .github/workflows/ci.yml sits on the R2 compliance path, and the reviewer for this CTO-authored compliance-path commit is the SecurityEngineer on a dedicated child review issue. No Reviewed-by trailer is written before that review actually happens.
whatTheChangeDoes: Adds staging to the CI push trigger in .github/workflows/ci.yml (branches: [main] -> [main, staging]), so post-merge pushes to the staging line re-run CI. One line changed, nothing else. Child of AFC-991 (staging-before-main): every PR already runs full CI (pull_request trigger has no branch filter) and the staging-before-main ruleset blocks merging to main/staging until all 8 checks pass; this line only covers post-merge pushes. No gate weakened, disabled, or made conditional; no secrets added; no application, migration, engine, or auth surface touched.
basis: Deployment & release lens: the staging line (origin/staging == origin/main at 7d36fe1) currently has no post-merge CI signal -- a push to staging after the AFC-991 merge runs zero checks, so a broken staging tip would be discovered only by the next PR or the timer. Risk lens: probability of drift is low (staging == main, timer no-ops) but impact is a silent red staging; the change is reversible (one line) and only adds CI runs on staging pushes (Cost lens: negligible -- a handful of extra runs per staging merge). Testing strategy lens: no new tests; the change is verified by the next staging push producing a green CI run. Observability lens: this restores the CI signal on the staging line rather than adding a new one.
verificationRecorded: Verified in an isolated worktree at origin/staging tip 7d36fe1 (detached, clean): diff is exactly one line in ci.yml plus this new claim file. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh --self-test passes on this tree. --check-commit on the landing commit must show R1 ok (Issue: AFC-1006 + this claim) and R2 via the SecurityEngineer review record; the R2 verdict and CI 8/8 green are recorded on the child review issue before landing.
